answer: In this agent economy, each participant must lock a durable basalt stake—hard, non-transferable tokens representing real resource commitment—secured by a rotating cipher that encrypts the stake identity. Over time, genuine agents accumulate relic attestations from successful interactions, which raise the economic threshold for new entrants. Attackers face escalating costs to forge multiple identities, as each fake requires fresh basalt stakes and cannot cheaply inherit relic history without breaking the cipher chain.
